# What collective common-frame programmes do, and do not, add

30 October 2026. Mathematical constructions and access-class lower bounds.
No quantum source, controller, optimizer, or new model instance is executed.
All traces and Choi states below are normalized unless stated otherwise.

The native memoryless source is

    N_U(x)=U(x tensor I_r/r)U*,  U:C^k tensor C^r -> C^D,
    U*U=I,  k>=2, D>=kr.                                      (1)

The target is a deterministic decoder for an independently supplied native
payload, including an arbitrary reference. Its error e is HALF diamond
distance from the logical identity, after composition with (1). Programme
acquisition in the classes treated here is independent of that payload.
The decoder can process the entire programme jointly with the payload.
This qualification is essential: payload-correlated future source queries
are not reduced to a calibration programme by the arguments below.

## 1. The whole reflection bank is an iid-Choi output

    J_U^tensor Q -> E_V [ |Psi_V><Psi_V|^tensor Q ],
    |Psi_V>=(I tensor V)|Phi_k>,                              (2)

where V:C^k->C^r tensor C^D is ONE Haar-random Stinespring frame of N_U.
There is no frame label. To verify the state/channel normalization, every
purification of J_U has reference marginal I_k/k. Reshaping it as the
normalized Choi vector of V therefore gives V*V=I. The Haar distributions

# Completed collective-programme boundary

30 October 2026. No new quantum/source or numerical scientific case run.

The entire common-frame reflection programme

    E_(V,theta)[(P_(V,theta)/k)^tensor Q]

is an EXACT CPTP output of Q iid normalized Choi copies. It is not merely
approximately simulated one reflection at a time. Therefore arbitrary
joint task-level processing of that bank cannot remove its quadratic-
rank copy obstruction. This includes full-throughput, all-reference
decoders of an independently supplied native flat mixed payload, provided
there are no additional original-source calls.

The explicit fixed-k entropy/concentration derivation gives

    Q >= r^2[log k-h(e)-e log(k-1)]/(16k^2),
    Q >= r^2[log 2-h(e)]/64  for k=2,

at HALF-diamond error e<1-1/k. The inherited k=3 proof was dimension-ported
in full; a three-label Fano claim is not being transplanted unchanged.
At fixed useful accuracy this matches the r exponent of the already
available O(k^2 r^2/epsilon) inverse WITHIN this bank class. It proves
neither its epsilon dependence nor its online depth optimal.

Two larger classes were acquired constructively:

* A known offline parallel query prestate with actual source-query
  marginal rho has iid-Choi simulation using
  Q ceil(chi/delta) copies, chi=k^Q||rho||_op. The entire post-query
  workspace can be retained. In particular chi=1 gives an exact Q-copy
  simulation, covering the literal RDS maximally mixed-input factory.

* A common-frame RDS programme with known product probe blocks of width
  <=b can be simulated with a FINITE common-frame Bell queue of at most
  ceil(Q k^(2b)/delta) copies, using only the supplied probe preparations
  and known Bell controls. The unconditional programme error is <=delta.
  All retries use ONE preacquired common-frame pool; no new frame is
  assumed to align. Arbitrary-known-matrix filters improve the copy-only
  cap to ceil(Q k^b/delta), or intrinsically
  ceil(sum_i m_i chi_i/delta). Their matrix acquisition is a separate cost.

Thus a bounded-width known-input construction still needs Omega(r^2)
queries at fixed k,b,error. The complete decoding error is e+delta+zeta
when a finite controller budget zeta is included, not merely the error
on a selected successful branch.

The decisive remaining interface is not improved processing of the same
bank: it is a genuinely different input/history res
